title: When I add a new service or environment, I want to automatically generate CI/CD pipeline configurati
job_to_be_done: When I add a new service or environment, I want to automatically generate CI/CD pipeline configuration files, so I can avoid configuration drift and repetitive edits.
painful_workflow: Manually duplicating workflow files, using environment variables, or templating with tools like copier or cookiecutter for each new environment and microservice.
current_workaround: Manually duplicating workflow files, using environment variables, or templating with tools like copier or cookiecutter.
verified_facts: SIG-0002 describes manual duplication/modification of CI/CD pipeline configuration files (e.g., GitHub Actions YAML) per new environment and microservice.
SIG-0002 states the trigger frequency as 'weekly to monthly' per new service or environment.
SIG-0002 lists current workarounds: manual duplication, environment variables, and templating with copier/cookiecutter.
SIG-0002 lists consequences: configuration drift, hard-to-debug build failures, repetitive edits, misconfiguration risk.
Cluster metadata confirms exactly 1 independent source and 1 source type (github-issues search).
inferences: The episodic trigger (weekly-to-monthly at best) implies low cumulative labor cost for most teams, undermining the economic case.
Because mature free and platform-native alternatives exist (reusable workflows, matrix builds, cookiecutter/copier, Backstage templates), most demand is likely absorbed without paid tooling.
The economic buyer for a hypothetical paid product is unclear — the affected user (developer) is typically not the purchaser.
The signal appears to be a synthesized workflow description rather than documented user complaints, suggesting the pain may be assumed rather than observed.
assumptions: That SIG-0002 reflects real user behavior rather than an analyst's generalization — no quotes or issue links are provided to confirm.
That teams actually add services/environments at the stated weekly-to-monthly cadence; many teams do so far less often.
That configuration drift from manual duplication actually materializes into debuggable failures at meaningful rates — asserted but not evidenced.
unknowns: Actual time cost per occurrence of duplicating/modifying pipeline configs.
Any quantified dollar impact or incident cost from configuration drift.
Whether any individual or organization has paid money to solve this specific problem.
The number and size of teams experiencing this pain at high frequency.
The specific GitHub issues, quotes, or discussions underlying SIG-0002.
Why existing free solutions (reusable workflows, copier/cookiecutter, Backstage) fail to adequately address the need.
